metadata.topic: Thermal Physics — Specific Heat Capacity and Power Rating

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q2b(ii/iii) — Calculate Specific Heat Capacity and Power Rating
question.text:
A group of students used an electrical method to calculate the specific heat capacity of a liquid. The students found that it took 400 s for the temperature of 0.2 kg of the liquid to be raised from 25 °C to 70 °C. The energy supplied by the immersion heater was 15.6 kJ during this period.

(ii) Calculate the value of the specific heat capacity of the liquid. Assume that no heat was lost and ignore the heat capacity of the container. (5 marks)

(iii) Calculate the power rating of the immersion heater. (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q2b(ii) — Specific Heat Capacity:

Formula: c = Q / (mΔθ)

Convert energy: Q = 15.6 kJ = 15 600 J

Temperature change: Δθ = 70 − 25 = 45 °C

c = 15 600 / (0.2 × 45) = 15 600 / 9 = 1 733 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹

Q2b(iii) — Power Rating:

Formula: P = E / t

P = 15 600 / 400 = 39 W

steps.label:
Given: m = 0.2 kg | θ_i = 25 °C | θ_f = 70 °C | Q = 15.6 kJ | t = 400 s
Formulas: c = Q/(mΔθ)  |  P = E/t
Calculate the specific heat capacity of the liquid. (5 marks)
Calculate the power rating of the immersion heater. (3 marks)

Subtract the initial temperature from the final temperature: Δθ = 70 − 25 = 45 °C.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use the specific heat capacity formula: c = Q / (m × Δθ), where Q is the energy in joules, m is the mass in kg, and Δθ is the temperature change in °C.
Use the power formula: P = E / t, where E is energy in joules and t is time in seconds.
